author: /root/learning_refinement
scope: A focused learning-hub refinement in the existing white/cobalt direction. No legal exercise, source, rule, session storage schema, canonical article or deployment changes.

implemented.result: The primary action resumes an unfinished curated step only within the selected path. Unrelated global last reading cannot replace that path’s next step. Completed starting steps lead to optional practice, then a path choice.

Choosing a different path pushes a shareable URL. Back/Forward restores the earlier selection. Same-path hash links retain their native Search/Practice navigation. Modifier clicks keep browser behavior. Cross-tab activity updates do not move the visible selected path.

The same eight path links are in a native disclosure rather than a large card detour. All 304 library links remain server-rendered in their existing native disclosure. No pagination, deletion, sign-in or practice gate was added. No-JavaScript path links target real fallback sections.

Search considers only existing public title, description and jurisdictions, requires every query token in any order, normalizes ordinary punctuation/diacritics, standard dotted U.S. and licence/license/licensing variants. Short/numeric terms match complete words. Matching rows show the existing public explanation.
A direct library jump focuses search; bookmark, started and no-match empty states explain the next action. Clear search and filters restores the library and input focus.

The initial path selection avoids a gratuitous progress write that would clear a corrupt-storage warning. Catalogue failure, cross-tab clearing, export/reset and separate planning storage retain their tested behavior.
Compact progress and the path disclosure bring selected content sooner. Mobile Read/Save controls have a 44px minimum height; no content was removed.

After corrupt progress is reported, explicitly opting in first copies the visible selected path into ephemeral progress, then saves it. The stable history listener reads the current storage error and active path, so Back/Forward still saves the correct selection after repair. Failed-catalogue persistence protection remains intact.

browser.target: isolated production build; temporary Node server 4322
browser.boundary: The13-case isolated build preceded the pure U.S. normalization and the final consent/history correction. The final helper passed unit cases; the final consent/history correction passed three targeted browser cases. Root will run the final combined release suite.

notes: Early dev runs found and resolved initial warning-clearing and same-path hash-scrolling regressions. The final browser run used isolated static output to avoid shared HMR and artifact-output races.

finalTargetedBrowser.scope: Final opt-in and repaired-storage Back/Forward regression, original selected-path history case, unavailable-catalogue saved-copy protection.
finalTargetedBrowser.target: Astro source preview on4321; root is rebuilding the final combined release separately.

limits: This author has not performed independent peer approval or deployment.
No new official rule, legal conclusion, real-business approval or source-review date is introduced.

A bare #learning-path-ID fragment by itself is not a JavaScript path selector. App-generated query-plus-fragment links and their native no-JavaScript fallback are supported and tested; the optional bare-fragment enhancement is deferred.
